title: Non-blocking findings from PR #318's review (backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-portfolio-risk-followups)
description: Non-blocking finding recorded by pr-reviewer's code-review pass on PR #318, tracked here per CLAUDE.md's 'every non-blocking finding becomes a tracked task' rule so it isn't lost once the PR merges.

checklist.step: docs/Analyse.md §7's 'Profit target' paragraph (line ~262) now ends '...See `app.portfolio.profit_target`'s own docstring and the `backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-portfolio-risk-followups` task's `decisions` entry for the full reasoning:' immediately followed by the Swing-style/Position-style bullet list. That colon's antecedent no longer matches what follows it: the bullets describe the two *implemented* target techniques, not 'the full reasoning' for why the third (day-trade divergence-exit) technique doesn't apply -- a reader following the colon expects the cross-referenced reasoning to continue there and instead finds an unrelated list. The pre-PR-318 wording didn't have this problem because its own list-introducing colon's antecedent ('the two [techniques] relevant to...') matched the list that followed it exactly. Reword so the cross-reference to the docstring/decisions entry no longer sits directly against the bullet-list colon -- e.g. move the 'See ... for the full reasoning' sentence to stand on its own (period, not colon) before a fresh sentence that introduces the two-techniques list, or restructure so the colon's antecedent is again the list itself.

decisions.decision: Fixed the dangling colon by splitting the cross-reference sentence from the list lead-in: '...for the full reasoning:' became '...for the full reasoning behind that gap. The two implemented techniques:' — leaving the docstring/decisions cross-reference as its own complete sentence (period) and adding a fresh short sentence whose antecedent ('the two implemented techniques') exactly matches the Swing-style/Position-style bullets that follow.
decisions.rationale: Considered moving the cross-reference sentence to after the bullet list instead (reordering), but that would separate it from the sentence introducing the day-trade-divergence-exit gap it explains, weakening the connection for a reader. Keeping it in place and just re-terminating it (period instead of colon) plus adding a short list-introducing sentence is the minimal edit that restores a matching colon antecedent without reflowing the paragraph or losing any existing content.
